exposure: Elevated serum bile acid levels (stratified as 10-39 micromole/lit and ≥40 micromole/lit)
outcome: APGAR score less than 7 at 1 min
APGAR score less than 7 at 5 min
cohort: The study included 50 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies, presenting with pruritus without dermatological conditions, and having elevated serum transaminases and serum bile acid levels in their late 2nd and 3rd trimesters, indicating intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy.
finding: Adverse foetal and maternal outcomes, including lower APGAR scores, low birth weight, and meconium-stained liquor, were significantly higher in women with serum bile acid levels of 40 micromole/lit and above.
mod_finding: 50% of the women in the study delivered by caesarean section, with the most common indications being foetal distress (32%) or meconium-stained liquor with foetal distress (28%).
birth_weight: Low birth weight was identified as an adverse outcome, significantly higher in the group with serum bile acid levels ≥40 micromole/lit.
gest_age: Preterm deliveries were an observed outcome, with participants included in the late 2nd and 3rd trimester of pregnancy.
